definition: A job position that is open and needs to be filled.
business_context_example: We have a vacancy for a part-time trainer starting in September.

definition: An advertisement describing an open position.
business_context_example: The job posting went live on Monday and we had 40 applications by Friday.

definition: A person who applies for a job.
business_context_example: Every applicant gets a reply, even if it's a no.

definition: The reduced list of the best candidates.
business_context_example: We shortlisted five people out of 40 applications.

definition: A short first interview to check basic suitability.
business_context_example: The screening call takes 15 minutes and covers salary expectations.

definition: An interview asking for examples of past behaviour.
business_context_example: In a competency-based interview, 'tell me about a time when' is the whole game.

definition: Contacting a candidate's former employer to confirm their record.
business_context_example: We do the reference check after the offer, not before.

definition: A written document offering someone a job.
business_context_example: The offer letter states the salary, start date and probation length.
translation_bg: предложение за работа в писмен вид

definition: The legal agreement between employer and employee.
business_context_example: Read the contract of employment before your first day, not after.

definition: An employment contract with an agreed end date.
business_context_example: It's a fixed-term contract covering maternity leave until next March.

definition: The non-salary rewards an employer offers.
business_context_example: The benefits package includes health insurance and a training budget.

definition: An increase in someone's salary.
business_context_example: She asked for a pay rise with three months of results in hand.

definition: Extra money paid for good performance or results.
business_context_example: The bonus is paid in February and depends on team targets.

definition: A plan for saving money for an employee's retirement.
business_context_example: The company matches your pension scheme contribution up to 5%.

definition: Paid holiday days an employee is entitled to each year.
business_context_example: You get 25 days of annual leave plus public holidays.

definition: Time off work to care for a new child.
business_context_example: He took four months of parental leave and nothing collapsed.

definition: Money paid to an employee who cannot work due to illness.
business_context_example: Sick pay starts on day one, not day four, in our policy.

definition: How often employees are away from work.
business_context_example: The absence rate doubled in the warehouse last winter.

definition: A system letting staff choose their start and finish times.
business_context_example: Flexitime means core hours are 10 to 3, the rest is yours.

definition: Extra time off given instead of payment for overtime.
business_context_example: You worked Saturday, so take time off in lieu on Tuesday.

definition: The rate at which employees leave and are replaced.
business_context_example: Staff turnover in the call centre is 60% a year.

definition: Keeping employees in the company rather than losing them.
business_context_example: Retention improved when we fixed the shift patterns, not the salaries.

definition: A questionnaire measuring how motivated staff feel.
business_context_example: The engagement survey said the same thing three years running.

definition: A meeting with an employee who is leaving, to learn why.
business_context_example: Three exit interviews mentioned the same manager.

definition: Officially telling your employer you are leaving.
business_context_example: She handed in her resignation on Monday morning.

definition: To formally tell your employer you are leaving.
business_context_example: He handed in his notice after eight years without a single warning sign.

definition: Losing a job because the position is no longer needed.
business_context_example: Redundancy is about the role, not the person, and that's worth saying out loud.

definition: Ending someone's employment because of their conduct or performance.
business_context_example: Dismissal requires a documented process, not a bad Friday.

definition: A formal complaint from an employee.
business_context_example: Any grievance goes in writing and gets a meeting within five days.

definition: The formal process for dealing with poor conduct.
business_context_example: The disciplinary procedure has three stages before dismissal.

definition: Behaviour that breaks the company's rules.
business_context_example: Sharing client data is gross misconduct, not a small mistake.

definition: A formal document recording that behaviour must change.
business_context_example: He received a written warning after the third late delivery.

definition: The written rules on how employees should behave.
business_context_example: Every new hire signs the code of conduct in week one.

definition: Reporting wrongdoing inside an organisation.
business_context_example: The whistleblowing policy promises no retaliation, in writing.

definition: Treating all people fairly regardless of background.
business_context_example: Equal opportunities means the same questions for every candidate.

definition: Building a workforce of different people who all feel they belong.
business_context_example: Diversity and inclusion training worked when managers went first.

definition: A healthy division between work and personal life.
business_context_example: Work-life balance is a policy question, not a personality question.
translation_bg: баланс между работа и личен живот

definition: Complete exhaustion caused by long-term work stress.
business_context_example: Two people went off with burnout in the same quarter.

definition: The amount of work a person has to do.
business_context_example: Her workload didn't change when two colleagues left, and that's the problem.

definition: Training and growth opportunities offered to staff.
business_context_example: Learning and development has its own budget line this year.

definition: To teach employees new abilities for their current job.
business_context_example: We upskilled the whole support team in written English.

definition: To train someone for a different role.
business_context_example: Two warehouse staff were reskilled into logistics planning.

definition: An experienced person who guides someone less experienced.
business_context_example: Every new manager gets a mentor for the first six months.

definition: The difference between skills you have and skills you need.
business_context_example: The skills gap is English, not technical knowledge.

definition: The planned steps of progress in someone's working life.
business_context_example: People stay when they can see a career path, even a slow one.

definition: To employ someone; also, a newly employed person.
business_context_example: We made four hires this quarter and lost one.

definition: A temporary worker.
business_context_example: We use a temp for the two busiest months.

definition: A document showing pay and deductions for a period.
business_context_example: Your payslip arrives by email on the 25th.

definition: Hours worked beyond normal working time.
business_context_example: Overtime is paid at 1.5 times the hourly rate.

definition: How content someone feels about their work.
business_context_example: Job satisfaction rose after we stopped the Friday reporting.
